objective: Determine whether Dial can reliably play an HTTPS internet-radio stream from an MCP Apps UI rendered inside ChatGPT.

reports.complexity: Low to medium for a bounded proof: one TypeScript MCP server with a deterministic known-station tool/resource and one minimal MCP Apps player; medium verification effort because host rendering, streaming, and lifecycle behavior require a reachable HTTPS endpoint and ChatGPT test host.
evidence: OpenAI official UI guidance says ChatGPT MCP Apps render in an iframe, use `_meta.ui.resourceUri` plus the `ui/*` bridge, and expose CSP allowlists for connect/resource/frame domains; source notes: evidence/triage-sources.md.
OpenAI UI guidance identifies PiP as a supported display mode for ongoing activity, including live sessions, but does not prove PiP works in this account or that native browser audio PiP applies.
OpenAI UI guidance distinguishes ephemeral UI instance state from durable cross-session state; the proof can explicitly document in-memory state and reset-on-remount behavior.

MCP TypeScript SDK guidance supports McpServer with Streamable HTTP for remote MCP hosts and stdio for local process-spawned integrations; Inspector CLI documents HTTP connection and tools/list/call/resource probes.
MCP Streamable HTTP is a single MCP endpoint with POST request/JSON-or-SSE responses; the radio media URL is a separate direct audio-element request from the UI.
MDN autoplay guidance establishes that audible media may be blocked absent user interaction; initiate play from the explicit Play click, catch play() rejection, and handle media error events.
Repository inspection found no product implementation. CUA returned empty browser/app inventories; REQUEST.md states no ChatGPT test connection or public HTTPS dev endpoint is established.
reports.handoff: Proceed directly to a bounded proof implementation; a separate full Spec is unnecessary because the criteria already fix the scope and observable behaviors. Use a TypeScript MCP server, remote Streamable HTTP for the ChatGPT-compatible endpoint, one known HTTPS stream, and a compact MCP Apps audio player with explicit Play/Pause/resume and visible error states. Use Inspector to verify the MCP tool/resource locally or over HTTP. Document that player state is ephemeral and lost on UI remount, list exact CSP/network observations, and investigate host PiP without expanding into persistence/product features. Keep ChatGPT host verification explicitly BLOCKED until endpoint and account access are available; do not reinterpret that block as a product requirement question.
open_questions: No product decision blocks implementation. The packet supplies a concrete one-station proof and all required behaviors; station selection and in-memory persistence semantics are narrow implementation choices.

Verification access blocker for Verify/Foreman: provide or establish a ChatGPT MCP Apps test connection and a publicly reachable HTTPS development endpoint before claiming iframe/audio/CSP/PiP success. This is access setup, not product ambiguity.
The host-specific media CSP rule and whether audio continues in ChatGPT PiP must be answered by the bounded live-host experiment.
relevant_code: No product code, TypeScript package manifest, MCP server, or UI currently exists in the DIAL-001 work item/repository files inspected; this task is greenfield proof scaffolding.

factory/work-items/DIAL-001/state.json and packets/run-5fc912079003.json: enumerate the exact acceptance criteria.
risks: The station endpoint may redirect, be intermittently unavailable, use an unsupported codec, or reject playback in the host; choose one stable HTTPS source and record exact endpoint/observed failure without implying general station compatibility.
ChatGPT iframe CSP/media policy and browser cross-origin behavior may prevent a station stream even where ordinary browser playback works; allowlists must be tested on the actual host.

Autoplay policy, network interruptions, and iframe remounts can make playback appear unreliable; start only on explicit user gesture, surface buffering/error states, and define resume as another user action.
PiP documentation establishes a host display mode, but availability and audio continuity while minimized remain empirical host checks.
reports.scope: Read-only feasibility and scope triage for the packet's one-station live HTTPS radio proof. Compared official ChatGPT MCP Apps documentation and MCP/Inspector transport guidance with repository contents and available verification surfaces.

ambiguities: ChatGPT iframe media CSP behavior, audible playback reliability, and PiP availability/audio continuity cannot be inferred from local tests or endpoint headers.
blockers: No connected ChatGPT test host or publicly reachable HTTPS development endpoint is available, so UI rendering in ChatGPT, audible Play/Pause/resume, media error presentation in the host, and PiP behavior remain unobserved. README.md gives exact manual checks for Verify.
reports.change_summary: Built a one-station TypeScript Streamable HTTP MCP server with an MCP Apps radio UI for Radio Paradise, explicit Play/Pause/resume and retryable error states, focused tests, and reproducible host verification notes.
decisions: Used Radio Paradise's HTTPS 128 kbps MP3 stream as the sole station; an HTTPS HEAD probe on 2026-10-03 returned 200 OK, audio/mpeg, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, and no redirect.
The audio element fetches the station stream directly. The UI resource declares the stream origin in resourceDomains and no connectDomains; host media CSP still requires live verification.
Player state is per UI instance and resets on remount. Resume rejoins the live stream; no durable state or background playback behavior is claimed.
Used the MCP Apps App bridge and versioned ui://dial/radio-v2.html for the bundled UI.
tests: npm test passed 4/4 on 2026-10-03 with localhost socket access: Play/Pause while buffering/resume, rejected play/media error retry, late rejection after Pause, and HTTP MCP connect/list/call/resource integration.

MCP Inspector CLI connected to http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp; tools/list returned open_radio with ui://dial/radio-v2.html; tools/call returned Radio Paradise with https://stream.radioparadise.com/mp3-128.
npm run build compiled TypeScript and bundled the browser UI; git diff --check passed before commit.
HTTPS HEAD probe of https://stream.radioparadise.com/mp3-128 returned HTTP 200, Content-Type audio/mpeg, and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *; this is network evidence, not audible playback evidence.

reports.architecture: Appropriately bounded: one stateless Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint, one deterministic station/tool, bundled HTML resource and small player controller. Installed ext-apps registration helpers and App.connect establish the intended bridge. Audio is fetched by the iframe, not proxied. No excluded search, accounts, database, favorites or deployment scope was added. Product files in the working tree match the exact candidate commit.
reports.complexity: Small production surface with direct media controls and no unnecessary persistence/framework. Existing dependency bundle is large but does not by itself justify scope expansion or block this proof. Fix the two narrow issues without adding a generalized player architecture.
reports.correctness: Play/Pause intent and attempt tokens correctly prevent late play-promise rejection from overwriting a paused/new attempt. Error text uses textContent and status is aria-live. The retained media-error retry defect is reproducible with a standard-informed double (R1), and live-edge resume is not implemented despite documentation (R2). Browser/ChatGPT execution and audible behavior were not observed.

findings.detail: After an initial source failure sets audio.error.code to MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED, Play only calls audio.play() again. That immediately rejects while the retained error remains, even after the source service recovers. The visible Try Play again advice cannot recover this state without remounting or externally changing src. The existing double never models retained errors.
findings.evidence: Independent persistent-error probe remained error with zero load calls. HTML Standard play algorithm rejects code 4 until the media load algorithm clears error: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-media-play .
findings.requested_change: On user retry after a media failure, run the media load/reset path before play, preserving synchronous user activation and attempt cancellation. Add a regression double whose play remains rejected until load clears the media error; retain rejection-race coverage.
findings.title: Reset the media element before retrying a failed source

findings.detail: README states that resume rejoins the live stream rather than resuming an archived position, but the controller only calls play on the paused element. It neither reloads the stream nor seeks to a live edge; buffered playback can resume from its prior position. The current call-count test does not prove the stronger timing claim.
findings.evidence: Candidate source inspection and HTML Standard internal play steps: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#dom-media-play . No actual stream timing observation was performed.
findings.requested_change: Either document same-element resume and explicitly leave live-edge timing to observation, or deliberately reconnect on resume and test that behavior. Do not claim live-edge rejoin from play alone.
findings.title: Align resume documentation with actual media behavior
